notes.text: Moses now returned to the door of the tabernacle, as an important supplicant for two favours, and prevails for both: herein he was a type of Christ the great intercessor, whom the Father heareth always. He is earnest with God for a grant of his presence with Israel in the rest of their march to Canaan. Thou sayst, bring up this people — Lord, it is thou thyself that employest me, and wilt thou not own me? I am in the way of my duty, and shall I not have thy presence with me in that way? Yet, Thou hast said, I know thee by name, as a particular friend, and thou hast also found grace in my sight, above any other.

Now therefore, if I have found grace in thy sight, shew me thy way — What favour God had expressed to the people they had forfeited the benefit of; and therefore Moses lays the stress of his plea upon what God had said to him. By this therefore he takes hold on God, Lord, if thou wilt do any thing for me, do this for the people. Thus our Lord Jesus, in his intercession, presents himself to the Father, as one in whom he is always well-pleased, and so obtains mercy for us with whom he is justly displeased, Shew me thy way, that I may know thee, that I may find grace in thy sight - He insinuates that the people also, though most unworthy, yet were in some relation to God; consider that this nation is thy people; a people that thou hast done great things for, redeemed to thyself, and taken into covenant with thyself; Lord, they are thy own, do not leave them.
And he said, If thy presence go not with me, carry us not up hence — He speaks as one that dreaded the thought of going forward without God's presence.

Wherein shall it be known to the nations that have their eyes upon us, that I, and thy people, have found grace in thy sight; so as to be separated from all people upon earth? Is it not that thou goest with us? Nothing short of that can answer these characters.

I will do this thing also that thou hast spoken — See the power of prayer! See the riches of God's goodness! See in type the prevalency of Christ's intercession, which he ever lives to make for all those that come to God by him! And the ground of that prevalency, is purely in his own merit, it is because thou hast found grace in my sight. And now God is perfectly reconciled to them, and his presence in the pillar of cloud returns to them.

I beseech thee shew me thy glory — Moses had lately been in the mount with God, and had had as intimate communion with God, as ever any man had on this side heaven, and yet he is still desiring a farther acquaintance. Shew me thy glory - Make me to see it; so the word is: make it some way or other visible, and enable me to bear the sight of it. Not that he was so ignorant as to think God's essence could be seen with bodily eyes, but having hitherto only heard a voice out of a pillar of cloud or fire, he desired to see some representation of the divine glory, such as God saw fit to gratify him with.

Thou canst not see my face — A full discovery of the glory of God would quite overpower the faculties of any mortal man. I will make all my goodness pass before thee - He had given him wonderful instances of his goodness in being reconciled to Israel; but that was only goodness in the stream, he would shew him goodness in the spring. This was a sufficient answer to his request: Shew me thy glory, saith Moses; I will shew thee my goodness, saith God. God's goodness is his glory; and he will have us to know him by the glory of his mercy, more than by the glory of his majesty. And I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious - In bestowing his gifts, and is not debtor to any, nor accountable to any; all his reasons of mercy are fetched from within himself, not from any merit in his creatures, and I will shew mercy on whom I will shew mercy - For his grace is always free. He never damns by prerogative, but by prerogative he saves.

I will put thee in a cleft of the rock — In that he was to be sheltered from the dazzling light, and devouring fire of God's glory. This was the rock in Horeb, out of which water was brought, of which it is said, That rock was Christ, 1 Cor. x, 4. 'Tis in the clefts of this rock that we are secured from the wrath of God, which otherwise would consume us: God himself will protect those that are thus hid: and it is only through Christ that we have the knowledge of the glory of God. None can see that to their comfort, but those that stand upon this rock, and take shelter in it.

And I will take away my hand — Speaking after the manner of men. And thou shalt see my back-parts - The face in man is the seat of majesty, and men are known by their faces, in them we take a full view of men; that sight of God Moses might not have, but such a sight as we have of a man who is gone past us, so that we only see his back. Now Moses was allowed to see this only, but when he was a witness to Christ's transfiguration, he saw his face shine as the sun. Four instances of the return of God's favour we have in this chapter. I. The orders he gives to Moses to come up to the mount the next morning, and bring two tables of stone with him, ver. 1-4. II. His meeting him there, and the proclamation of his name, ver. 6-9. III. The instructions he gave him there, and his converse with him forty days, ver. 10-28. IV. The honour he put upon him when he sent him down with his face shining, ver. 29-35. In all which God dealt with Moses as a mediator between him and Israel, and a type of the great Mediator.

glossa.text: *And thee thyself I have known,* etc. *((AUG., quaest. 153.)) Because I know thee above all men,* etc. Does God know some things more and some things less? etc., *as far as* but it is to be sought more diligently in the earlier parts of Scripture whether it be truly so.

*I will show. ((AUG., quaest. 154.))* When Moses had said to the Lord, etc., *as far as* the Lord Christ is called upon among all nations.

*And I will call. ((AUG., quaest. 154.)) I will call,* however, he said, not "I shall be called," putting an active verb for a passive, by an unwonted manner of speech, in which perhaps he willed to signify that he himself does this, that is, that it comes about by his grace that the Lord is called upon among all nations.

*And I will have mercy,* etc. ((AUG., ubi supra. )) That which he added, etc., *as far as* thus God declared that he would show mercy.

((AUG., lib. de Praedestinatione et Gratia, cap. 10.)) That men are called by God with no merits going before, etc., *as far as* if he who called should forsake them.

*Thou shalt not be able,* etc. ((AUG., quaest. 154.)) After the commendation of his mercy, etc., *as far as* one must die to this life.
*For not,* etc. ((GREG., lib. XVIII Moral., cap. 37, tom. I.)) John also says: etc., *as far as* because satiety is ever kindled out of desire.

*Behold,* he says, *there is a place with me, and thou shalt stand upon,* etc. ((AUG., quaest. 154.)) Again, when Scripture interposes the article and says, etc., *as far as* the faithful people stood upon the rock.

*((GREG., lib. XXV Moral., cap. 16.)) There is a place with me,* etc. The place is the Church. The rock is the Lord; Moses, the Jewish people, which did not believe the Lord preaching upon earth. It therefore stood upon the rock, beholding the back parts of the Lord as he passed by, because, that is, after the passion and ascension of the Lord, being led within the Church, it deserved to receive Christ by faith, and of him whose presence it did not see, it came to know the hinder parts.

*((GREG. ibid.)) There is a place with me,* etc. The Church, namely, etc., *as far as* Of which solidity it is said: *Upon this rock I will build the Church.*

*And when my glory shall pass,* etc. ((EUCHERIUS, lib. de Form. spirit.)) But God is said also to pass over, when out of the hearts of certain men, in which he was before believed by faith, afterwards, faithlessness creeping in or some offence whatever, he withdraws from them and passes over to others: as from the Jews to the Gentiles, from heretics to Catholics, and from any irreligious persons whatever to the religious.

*And I will protect* ((AUG., ubi supra. )) *and I will cover with my hand over thee,* etc. , *as far as* then he weaves in what the Lord says afterwards: *Hew thee two tables of stone,* etc.

notes.text: People — Such as are enemies to God and his people. Sitteth - Upon the ark. He is present with his people. Earth - The people of the earth. Moved - With fear and trembling.
Them — All people.

Judgment — Though his dominion be absolute, and his power irresistible, yet he manages it with righteousness. The king's strength is by a known Hebraism put for the strong, or powerful king. Equity - In all thy proceedings.
Foot-stool — Before the ark, which is so called, 1 Chron. xxviii, 2. Holy - It is consecrated to be a pledge of God's presence.
Moses — Moses before the institution of the priesthood executed that office, Exod. xxiv, 6. That call - Who used frequently and solemnly to intercede with God on the behalf of the people.
Spake — To some of them: to Moses and Aaron, Exod. xix, 24; xxxiii, 9-11; 1 Sam. vii, 9, &c.

Them — The intercessors before mentioned. Forgavest - The people for whom they prayed, so far as not to inflict that total destruction upon them which they deserved; An exhortation to praise God and to rejoice in him, ver. 1- 5 A psalm of praise This psalm was composed by David between the time of God's promising the kingdom to him and his actual possession of it. The general scope of David's vow, at his entrance on his government, ver. 1, 2. The particulars of it, ver. 3-8. A psalm of David.

glossa.text: *A psalm of David.* ((AUG.)) The prophet describes Christ the king giving good things, etc., *as far as* but the veil has been taken away, since *truth is sprung out of the earth, and justice hath looked down from heaven ((Psal. XLVIII))*. *The Lord hath reigned* ((CASS.)) Concerning the power and the kingdom of Christ, that he may be adored in the man. He shows Christ reigning, and (whosoever may resist) high above all, whence he admonishes to yield to him. *Let the peoples be angry.* ((CASS.)) A derision. It can safely be granted that they be angry, because they are not going to hurt any further: he speaks by permitting, not by commanding. *He sitteth upon the cherubim.* ((ID.)) Against him the earth can do nothing, even though he himself was on the earth where he suffered the wrath of the people. *Cherubim.* ((AUG.)) *The fulness of knowledge* is its interpretation, which is charity. The fulness of the knowledge of the law, which is the seat of God, shall be in thee also, if thou hast charity, against which the angry can do nothing. For what is the earth against heaven?

*The Lord in Sion.* ((ID.)) If thou dost not understand what is *upon the Cherubim,* see this, that he is *great in Sion.* Sion is the soul which beholds God. *Great in Sion.* ((CASS.)) Who the Lord is, he sets forth: *In Sion* born. *Great,* lest he grow cheap on account of the passion. Or, yet the Lord is great in the Sion of the Jews, and above the peoples of the Gentiles.

*Great.* ((AUG.)) It was little when they were angry, that is, made known among few, but now enlarged in all the earth. *Terrible.* ((ID.)) Because even if he is preached as crucified, he is the judge to come, and he shall not err in judgment. *And the honor of the king.* ((CASS.)) He sets forth how they ought to confess. *The honor of the king,* is the glorious preaching, *judgment* requires discernment; he is to be worshipped not with a light will, but with fixed deliberation, which is from him; whence he subjoins: *Thou hast prepared directions.* Or *the honor of the king* is the damnation of the guilty, whereby the glory of the king is increased.
*In Jacob.* ((AUG.)) Not only the patriarch, but the people whom he signifies. *Thou hast done.* These things, which another could not do.

*Exalt ye.* ((CASS.)) The second part admonishes to adore him, because his fathers *were.* As it were, because he does these things for us, therefore *Exalt ye.*

*The footstool.* ((AUG.)) *The earth is the footstool of his feet,* says Scripture, etc., *as far as* in whose honor it adores the footstool. *Of the feet.* ((CASS.)) *The feet,* the unfailing stability of the Godhead. *Holy.* That thou mayest distinguish the body from the Godhead, even though it be one person.
*Moses.* ((CASS.)) A priest, because if not victims, he offered the vows of the people, and made supplication for the people.

*A pillar.* ((CASS.)) The strength and the beauty of the house. In this appearance he spoke, which announced the Church, or the flesh, but then in a cloud, now openly through the Son: *He spoke to them out of the cloud.* ((ID.)) To them therefore then in a cloud, who now speaks to us in the footstool, that is, openly in the flesh assumed. *His testimonies and precepts.* ((ID.)) A testimony is a signification set down by certain signs of a preceding thing: whence often in the law it is said: *This shall be to you for a testimony.* The precepts are as the precepts of the law given through Moses.

*Thou wast merciful to them.* ((AUG.)) It is not said save of sins, merciful in forgiving, merciful also in avenging, behold, even though these were so great, yet they had somewhat of sin; whence he adds, *upon all their inventions.*

*Avenging.* Lest human elation should creep upon them; whence: There was given me a sting of my flesh *((II Cor. XII)) Inventions.* Otherwise, affections. ((AUG.)) Which God alone knew in their hearts; whence it was a punishment to them to bear with those among whom they were, for whose sins they grieved as for their own, through charity. For it was not, as is thought by very many, a punishment to Moses not to enter into the land of promise, into which the wretched also entered; but a figure, that they who were under the law, and were unwilling to be under grace, should not enter into rest.

notes.text: His desire, 17-20
His care, iii. 1-5

His joy and prayer for them, 6-13 IV. He exhorts them to grow,

1. In holiness, iv.1-8

2. In brotherly love with industry, 9-12 V. He teaches and exhorts,

1. Concerning them that sleep, 13-18

2. Concerning the times, v.1-11 VI. He adds miscellaneous exhortations, 12-24 VII. The conclusion, 25-28 1 THESSALONIANS
Knowing your election — Which is through faith, by these plain proofs.

With power — Piercing the very heart with a sense of sin and deeply convincing you of your want of a saviour from guilt, misery, and eternal ruin. With the Holy Ghost - Bearing an outward testimony, by miracles, to the truth of what we preached, and you felt: also by his descent through laying on of hands. With much assurance - Literally, with full assurance, and much of it: the Spirit bearing witness by shedding the love of God abroad in your hearts, which is the highest testimony that can be given. And these signs, if not the miraculous gifts, always attend the preaching of the gospel, unless it be in vain: neither are the extraordinary operations of the Holy Ghost ever wholly withheld, where the gospel is preached with power, and men are alive to God. For your sake - Seeking your advantage, not our own.
Though in much affliction, yet with much joy.

For from you the word sounded forth — (Thessalonica being a city of great commerce.) Being echoed, as it were, from you. And your conversion was divulged far beyond Macedonia and Achaia. So that we need not speak anything - Concerning it.
For they themselves — The people wherever we come.

Whom he hath raised from the dead — In proof of his future coming to judgment. Who delivereth us - He redeemed us once; he delivers us continually; and will deliver all that believe from the wrath, the eternal vengeance, which will then come upon the ungodly.

glossa.text: *Silvanus and Timothy.* The salutation is prefixed with their names, but the sense and the words of this epistle are the Apostle's alone.

*Grace be to you and peace.* After his custom he sets the salutation first, and this being set first, he gives thanks for their good things, calling to mind not only their faith and works, but also the manner of their conversion and their endurance of evils.
*Before God.* Thence [you are] so certain as though you already saw; and thus he encourages them.

*In the Holy Spirit.* Because through me you received the gifts of the Spirit, not sparingly, but in fullness. *What manner of men we were,* etc. By this also, that we have suffered for an example to you, it is plain that God has loved and chosen you.

notes.text: Mark xii, 13; Luke xx, 20.

The Herodians were a set of men peculiarly attached to Herod, and consequently zealous for the interest of the Roman government, which was the main support of the dignity and royalty of his family. Thou regardest not the person of men — Thou favourest no man for his riches or greatness.

Is it lawful to give tribute to Caesar? — If he had said, Yes, the Pharisees would have accused him to the people, as a betrayer of the liberties of his country. If he had said, No, the Herodians would have accused him to the Roman governor.
Ye hypocrites — Pretending a scruple of conscience.
The tribute money — A Roman coin, stamped with the head of Caesar, which was usually paid in tribute.

They say to him, Caesar's — Plainly acknowledging, by their having received his coin, that they were under his government. And indeed this is a standing rule. The current coin of every nation shows who is the supreme governor of it. Render therefore, ye Pharisees, to Caesar the things which ye yourselves acknowledge to be Ciaesar's: and, ye Herodians, while ye are zealous for Caesar, see that ye render to God the things that are God's.

glossa.text:
*With the Herodians, saying.* As though to men unknown, that they might the more easily deceive, because they feared the crowds. What they dare not by themselves, they attempt by the governor's hands. *With the Herodians.* That is, with the soldiers of Herod. Under Caesar Augustus, when the enrolment was made, Judea was made tributary. Over these tributes was set Herod the son of Antipater, an alien and a proselyte, appointed king for the Jews by Augustus. There was therefore sedition among the people, some saying that tributes ought to be given, for security and quiet, since the Romans bear arms for all. The Pharisees striving against it, that the people of God, which pays tithes and the rest that the law prescribes, ought not to lie under human laws. The Pharisees therefore send to see whether they might deceive him.

*Thou hast no care,* etc. To this they provoke him, that he should fear God more than Caesar: and therefore should say that tributes ought not to be paid, so that the Herodians might hold him as the author of sedition.
*Hypocrites.* Because they are one thing and feign another.
*Render therefore.* Or, as Caesar exacts the stamping of his own image, so also does God the soul signed with the light of his countenance.

echoes.text: ‘Yahweh bless you, and keep you. Yahweh make his face to shine on you, and be gracious to you. Yahweh lift up his face toward you, and give you peace.’
echoes.note: Paul's epistolary 'Grace to you and peace' fuses a Greek salutation with the Hebrew shalom; the doubled blessing of grace/favor and peace recalls the Aaronic benediction where YHWH makes his face shine (grace) and gives peace. Volume is low and the wording is Pauline convention, so the echo is faint, but Availability and Coherence with a Jewish blessing idiom support a thin resonance.

echoes.text: Yes, in the way of your judgments, Yahweh, have we waited for you. Your name and your renown are the desire of our soul.
echoes.note: The triad work-of-faith, labor-of-love, and 'patience (endurance) of hope' before God resonates with Isaiah's posture of waiting for YHWH's name in the path of his judgments, the soul's desire and hope. The conceptual overlap (steadfast hope directed toward God) is real but the verbal volume is minimal, so this is a contested coherence-driven echo.

echoes.text: For you are a holy people to Yahweh your God. Yahweh your God has chosen you to be a people for his own possession, above all peoples who are on the face of the earth. Yahweh didn’t set his love on you, nor choose you, because you were more in number than any people; for you were the fewest of all peoples: but because Yahweh loves you, and because he desires to keep the oath which he swore to your fathers, Yahweh has brought you out with a mighty hand, […]
echoes.note: 'Brothers loved by God, that you are chosen' transposes Israel's covenant election directly: Deuteronomy says YHWH chose Israel not for their merit but because he loved them (agapan/eklegesthai LXX), the exact pairing of divine love and choosing Paul applies to gentile believers. Volume and Coherence are strong, and Recurrence of the election theme through 1 Thess makes this a programmatic allusion.

echoes.text: Blessed is the nation whose God is Yahweh, the people whom he has chosen for his own inheritance.
echoes.note: 'Blessed is the nation whose God is YHWH, the people he has chosen for his own inheritance' supplies the same election idiom Paul extends to the Thessalonian assembly. The LXX exelexato matches Paul's vocabulary of being chosen; Volume is moderate and the allusion reinforces the Deuteronomic election frame.

echoes.text: “But you, Israel, my servant, Jacob whom I have chosen, the seed of Abraham my friend, You whom I have taken hold of from the ends of the earth, and called from its corners, and said to you, ‘You are my servant, I have chosen you and not cast you away;’
echoes.note: 'Israel my servant, Jacob whom I have chosen, offspring of Abraham my beloved... I have chosen you and not cast you off' clusters chosenness and divine love exactly as Paul does. The dense overlap of election + beloved makes this a plausible secondary source alongside Deuteronomy 7.

echoes.text: The Spirit of the Lord Yahweh is on me; because Yahweh has anointed me to preach good news to the humble. He has sent me to bind up the broken hearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives, and release to those who are bound;
echoes.note: The gospel coming 'not in word only, but also in power and in the Holy Spirit' echoes the Spirit-anointed proclamation of good news (the LXX euangelisasthai with the Spirit of the Lord upon the herald). Coherence with Paul's evangel-in-Spirit is strong; verbal volume is moderate, supporting an echo of the Isaianic herald.
echoes.lxxText: The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he has anointed me; he has sent me to preach glad tidings to the poor, to heal the broken in heart, to proclaim liberty to the captives, and recovery of sight to the blind;

echoes.text: About Benjamin he said, “The beloved of Yahweh will dwell in safety by him. He covers him all day long. He dwells between his shoulders.”
echoes.note: 'Beloved of YHWH' (Benjamin) as a covenant epithet underlies Paul's address 'brothers loved by God.' The phrase is a stock Septuagintal way of naming the elect community; faint by itself but coherent with the surrounding election language.

echoes.text: But as for me, I am full of power by the Spirit of Yahweh, and of judgment, and of might, to declare to Jacob his disobedience, and to Israel his sin.
echoes.note: 'I am full of power by the Spirit of YHWH' pairs power and Spirit as the equipment of true proclamation, the same coupling Paul uses to validate his preaching against mere word. The dyad is suggestive but the link is contested given how common power/Spirit language is.

echoes.text: Therefore with joy you will draw water out of the wells of salvation.
echoes.note: 'Received the word in much affliction, with joy of the Holy Spirit' resonates with the prophetic motif of drawing joy from God amid distress (e.g., joy from the wells of salvation). The eschatological-Spirit joy-in-affliction pattern is broadly Septuagintal; volume is low, so this is a faint coherence echo.

echoes.text: Many peoples shall go and say, “Come, let’s go up to the mountain of Yahweh, to the house of the God of Jacob; and he will teach us of his ways, and we will walk in his paths.” For out of Zion the law shall go out, and Yahweh’s word from Jerusalem.
echoes.note: 'From you the word of the Lord has been declared... in every place' echoes the Zion oracle in which the word of YHWH goes forth from Jerusalem to the nations. Paul recasts the believing community as a new radiating center for the logos kyriou; Coherence with the mission-of-the-word theme is strong though the geography is reapplied.

echoes.text: so shall my word be that goes out of my mouth: it shall not return to me void, but it shall accomplish that which I please, and it shall prosper in the thing I sent it to do.
echoes.note: YHWH's word that 'goes out' from his mouth and does not return empty but accomplishes its purpose underlies the image of the word of the Lord sounding forth and bearing fruit everywhere. The 'going out' verb and effectual-word theology cohere, but the verbal contact is modest.

echoes.text: Their voice has gone out through all the earth, their words to the end of the world. In them he has set a tent for the sun,
echoes.note: 'Their voice has gone out into all the earth' is the classic text for a proclamation diffusing universally (cited at Romans 10:18). The 'gone out into every place' phrasing of Paul's report shares this diffusion imagery; faint but availability and coherence warrant noting.

echoes.text: For from the rising of the sun even to the going down of the same, my name is great among the nations, and in every place incense will be offered to my name, and a pure offering: for my name is great among the nations,” says Yahweh of Armies.
echoes.note: 'In every place' offerings are made to YHWH's name 'from the rising of the sun to its setting' supplies the universalizing 'in every place' formula Paul uses for the spread of faith toward God. The phrase is a Septuagintal marker of the name's worldwide honor; contested given its commonness.

echoes.text: But Yahweh is the true God; he is the living God, and an everlasting King: at his wrath the earth trembles, and the nations are not able to withstand his indignation.
echoes.note: 'A living and true God' set against 'idols' renders Jeremiah's contrast: 'YHWH is the true God; he is the living God' over against the worthless idols of the nations. Jeremiah 10 is the locus classicus of the idol-polemic Paul compresses; Volume, Coherence, and the living/true pairing make this a strong allusion.

echoes.text: Their idols are silver and gold, the work of men’s hands. They have mouths, but they don’t speak. They have eyes, but they don’t see. They have ears, but they don’t hear. They have noses, but they don’t smell. They have hands, but they don’t feel. They have feet, but they don’t walk, neither do they speak through their throat. Those who make them will be like them; yes, everyone who trusts in them.
echoes.note: 'You turned to God from idols' draws on the satire of manufactured idols (silver and gold, the work of human hands, with mouths that cannot speak) versus the living God. The turning-from-idols-to-serve-God movement is the Psalm's polemic inverted into conversion language; high coherence and strong Septuagintal availability.

echoes.text: Everyone who makes an engraved image is vain. The things that they delight in will not profit. Their own witnesses don’t see, nor know, that they may be disappointed. Who has fashioned a god, or molds an image that is profitable for nothing? Behold, all his fellows will be disappointed; and the workmen are mere men. Let them all be gathered together. Let them stand up. They will fear. They will be put to shame together. The blacksmith takes an ax, works […]
echoes.note: Isaiah's extended mockery of idol-makers who fashion lifeless gods is the deutero-Isaianic counterpart Paul presupposes in 'turned to God from idols.' The dead-idols vs. living-God antithesis is the engine of the verse; Recurrence of this polemic across Second-Temple Judaism strengthens the allusion.

echoes.text: That day is a day of wrath, a day of distress and anguish, a day of trouble and ruin, a day of darkness and gloom, a day of clouds and blackness,
echoes.note: 'The wrath to come' from which Jesus delivers draws on the Day of YHWH as 'a day of wrath' (the orge of the Lord); Zephaniah 1:15,18 is the densest concentration of day-of-wrath language Paul presupposes for the coming eschatological judgment. Coherence with Pauline orge and Recurrence of the wrath motif in 1 Thess (2:16; 5:9) make this a primary allusion.

echoes.text: I make a decree, that in all the dominion of my kingdom men tremble and fear before the God of Daniel; for he is the living God, and steadfast forever, His kingdom that which shall not be destroyed; and his dominion shall be even to the end.
echoes.note: Darius's decree that all should fear 'the living God... who endures forever' supplies the 'living God' confession that gentiles are summoned to serve. The phrase 'living God' is the verbal anchor; Daniel's gentile-king acknowledgment coheres with Paul's report of gentile turning to the living and true God.

echoes.text: You shall fear Yahweh your God; and you shall serve him, and shall swear by his name.
echoes.note: 'To serve a living and true God' picks up the Shema-context command to fear YHWH and serve (latreuein) him only, the exclusive-service demand that idolatry violates. The Deuteronomic 'serve him alone' is the positive correlate of turning from idols; coherence is strong, volume moderate.

echoes.text: Neither their silver nor their gold will be able to deliver them in the day of Yahweh’s wrath, but the whole land will be devoured by the fire of his jealousy; for he will make an end, yes, a terrible end, of all those who dwell in the land.
echoes.note: 'In the day of YHWH's wrath... the whole earth shall be consumed' supplies the universal, future, fiery character of 'the wrath to come.' Reinforces 1:15 as the Day-of-the-Lord matrix from which deliverance is needed.

echoes.text: Yahweh thunders his voice before his army; for his forces are very great; for he is strong who obeys his command; for the day of Yahweh is great and very awesome, and who can endure it?
echoes.note: 'The day of YHWH is great and very terrible; who can endure it?' frames the coming wrath as the dreadful Day from which one must be rescued. Joel's rhetorical question about enduring the Day undergirds Paul's promise that Jesus 'delivers us'; coherence is strong, verbal volume moderate.

echoes.text: Behold, the day of Yahweh comes, cruel, with wrath and fierce anger; to make the land a desolation, and to destroy its sinners out of it.
echoes.note: 'The day of YHWH comes, cruel, with wrath and fierce anger, to make the earth a desolation' is a paradigmatic Day-of-wrath oracle feeding Paul's 'wrath to come.' The eschatological orge directed at the nations coheres with the deliverance of believers; a solid secondary source for the wrath motif.

echoes.text: “But who can endure the day of his coming? And who will stand when he appears? For he is like a refiner’s fire, and like launderer’s soap;
echoes.note: 'Who can endure the day of his coming?' couples the coming (the One who comes) with refining judgment, resonating with waiting for the Son who delivers from the coming wrath. The 'who can endure' topos and the link of advent + judgment make this a coherent echo within the Day-of-the-Lord cluster.

echoes.text: Now for a long time Israel was without the true God, and without a teaching priest, and without law.
echoes.note: 'For a long time Israel was without the true God' uses the precise phrase 'true God' that Paul applies to the object of conversion. A faint but genuine Septuagintal source for 'true God' alongside Jeremiah 10.

echoes.text: Come, my people, enter into your rooms, and shut your doors behind you. Hide yourself for a little moment, until the indignation is past. For, behold, Yahweh comes out of his place to punish the inhabitants of the earth for their iniquity. The earth also will disclose her blood, and will no longer cover her slain.
echoes.note: 'Hide yourselves... until the wrath (orge) is past, for YHWH comes out to punish' offers the motif of being sheltered from passing wrath, paralleling deliverance 'from the wrath to come.' Faint verbal contact but apt coherence with rescue-from-wrath; contested.

echoes.text: I will tell of the decree. Yahweh said to me, “You are my son. Today I have become your father.
echoes.note: 'To wait for his Son from heaven' reads the enthroned royal Son ('You are my Son') figurally of the risen Jesus whose advent executes divine judgment, the Psalm whose next verses warn the nations of the Son's wrath. The Son-language plus impending judgment coheres figurally, though Paul does not cite it here; marked low and contested.

echoes.text: I saw in the night visions, and behold, there came with the clouds of the sky one like a son of man, and he came even to the ancient of days, and they brought him near before him.
echoes.note: Waiting for the Son to come 'from heaven' to deliver at the judgment evokes the one like a son of man coming with the clouds to receive dominion at the eschatological assize. The heavenly-advent-and-judgment pattern is figurally apposite, though the explicit Son-of-Man title is absent here; faint, contested.

echoes.attribution: Catena, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wilson Pruitt / Wroot Press)

echoes.text: God created man in his own image. In God’s image he created him; male and female he created them.
echoes.note: Jesus' question 'whose image (eikon) and inscription?' (22:20) plays on imago Dei: the coin bears Caesar's image and is owed to Caesar, but humanity bears God's image and is owed wholly to God — 'render to God the things that are God's' (22:21).

echoes.text: The earth is Yahweh’s, with its fullness; the world, and those who dwell therein.
echoes.note: 'The earth is the LORD's, and the fulness thereof' — undergirds the claim that what is God's (everything, including the bearer of his image) belongs to God (22:21).

echoes.text: I say, “Keep the king’s command!” because of the oath to God.
echoes.note: Counsel to keep the king's commandment because of one's oath to God — faint wisdom backdrop to the dual obligation to Caesar and to God (22:21).

notes.text: His anointed — His king, whom God has designed, and separated, and fitted, in all respects, for this work. Loose - I will take away their girdle, which was about their loins; their power and authority, whereof that was an ensign. Gates - The great and magnificent gates of their cities and palaces, which shall be opened to him as conqueror.
Go — To remove all obstructions, to destroy all them that oppose thee, and carry thee through the greatest difficulties.
The treasures — Such as have been long kept in dark and secret places.
I have — I knew, and called thee by thy name, when thou didst neither know nor think of me; nay, when thou hadst no being.
I girded — I made thee strong and active, and disposed thee for these great and warlike enterprizes.

That — That all nations may know it by my foretelling these things so long before, and by the wonderful success that I shall give thee, and by my over-ruling thine heart and counsels, to the deliverance of my people.
Light — All mens comforts and calamities come from thy hand.

glossa.text:
*Thus says the Lord to his Christ.* Among the Romans the diadem, among the Jews the anointing, makes both kings and priests, from which they are also called christs. Cyrus is a christ, not by anointing, but by dignity.

*And the backs of kings.* ((ID.)) What city did not lie open to him? Which of the kings did not turn his back? What walls, before impregnable, were not overthrown by his siege? But you will find these things more fully fulfilled in the history of Xenophon.
*Hidden treasures.* Of all the cities, so that, having cast away idols, and invited by benefits, thou mightest perceive one God, who foretold thy name beforehand, before thou wert.
*And I have called thee.* ((ID.)) As I called Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, etc., *as far as* but the Son, Christ, is anointed with the oil of gladness above his fellows.
*Beside me.* Because the Son and the Holy Spirit are in the Father; for beside my word and my reason and my power and the wisdom that is in me, there is no other God.

*That they may know.* Esdras says that Cyrus wrote to all the nations that there is no God but the God of Israel. Or, from the freeing of the captives the clemency and power of God became better known to all. Josephus, moreover, in the book of the *Antiquities* says that the people was released for this reason, that Cyrus read in the book of Isaiah the things which the Lord had said of him before through the prophet.

*Darkness.* The night, or the captivity. As if: taking pity on the penitent, I bring them back from captivity; being angry, I take sinners captive.

*Evil.* ((ID.)) War, that is, affliction, according to what is said: Sufficient for the day is its own evil. Let them therefore be confounded who judge God to be the author of evils. For here evil is set down not as the contrary of good, but for affliction and for war.

notes.text: O sing — Upon this new and great occasion, not the removal of the ark, but the coming of the Messiah.
Gods — The gods of the nations, as the next verse expounds it.
Before him — In his presence.
Beauty — Cloathed with all the gifts and graces, which are necessary in God's worship.

glossa.text: *Sing ye to the Lord.* ((ID.)) He forewarned the Jews in the preceding psalm that, their hardness being laid aside, they should believe Christ; but because it was to abide, he now admonishes all the Gentiles. The second psalm concerning both comings. First he speaks to the prelates, that they themselves should sing and declare. *A new canticle.* ((AUG.)) Cupidity sings the *old,* etc., *as far as* whosoever shall have entered in, is without.

*To the Lord, and bless.* ((HIER., CASS.)) Thrice to the Lord, for the distinguishing of the trinity of persons; because the praise of Christ is the honor of the Trinity. And there is the figure epimone, that is, a frequent repetition of the same sentiment, which heightens it unto praise or unto blame.

*Declare ye.* He speaks to the prelates, declare, because thus grows the building of the house. *From day to day.* ((CASS.)) The Old and the New Testament are days, which grow bright by the eternal sun, the one foretells, the other shows the thing done. ((HIER.)) He declares therefore from day to day, etc., *as far as* by which the feet of our affections are fenced from the thorns of the vices.
*Great is the Lord.* ((AUG.)) Made little, because you are little, understand him great, and you shall be great in him.
*He made the heavens.* ((ID.)) The apostles and the angels, whence if he made the heavens and the angels, then the apostles also, who command the demons.

*In the sight.* For such men, namely those confessing and just, behold him themselves, and are beheld by him. *Holiness and magnificence.* ((AUG.)) As if he should say: He who wishes to be magnificent and mighty, as the angels are, let him first be holy, which comes to pass from him who sanctifies: for of thyself thou canst not be holy. When therefore he sanctifies, a man is made holy, and so magnificent.

*Bring to the Lord, ye kindreds.* ((CASS.)) The second part, where he speaks to the subjects, etc., *as far as* that none be excepted, native or stranger. *Glory.* ((ID.)) Because a man converses well, in whom God is glorified. *Honor.* When from good things thanks are rendered, whence, *There was not found who would give honor to God, but this stranger. Into the courts.* ((ID.)) The *courts,* the prophets or the apostles, by whom there is a going to the Lord; from the courts, that is, the prophets or the apostles, there is a coming into the court of the Catholic Church, where the majesty is adored. ((AUG.)) Or, Enter ye into the court, that is, into the doctrine of the prophets and the apostles.

*Adore ye the Lord in the court,* etc. That is, in the Catholic Church, or by the *courts,* prophecy; by the *court,* the Gospel. *Let it be moved.* All being admonished, he desires that they be moved. As if he should say, enter in and adore, you that are good. *But the earth,* etc. *The whole earth.* ((CASS.)) Not some part of it; therefore, lest anyone say: *Lo, here is Christ to be there,* he subjoins, *For he hath corrected the world of the earth,* etc.

notes.text: His desire, 17-20
His care, iii. 1-5

His joy and prayer for them, 6-13 IV. He exhorts them to grow,

1. In holiness, iv.1-8

2. In brotherly love with industry, 9-12 V. He teaches and exhorts,

1. Concerning them that sleep, 13-18

2. Concerning the times, v.1-11 VI. He adds miscellaneous exhortations, 12-24 VII. The conclusion, 25-28 1 THESSALONIANS
Knowing your election — Which is through faith, by these plain proofs.

With power — Piercing the very heart with a sense of sin and deeply convincing you of your want of a saviour from guilt, misery, and eternal ruin. With the Holy Ghost - Bearing an outward testimony, by miracles, to the truth of what we preached, and you felt: also by his descent through laying on of hands. With much assurance - Literally, with full assurance, and much of it: the Spirit bearing witness by shedding the love of God abroad in your hearts, which is the highest testimony that can be given. And these signs, if not the miraculous gifts, always attend the preaching of the gospel, unless it be in vain: neither are the extraordinary operations of the Holy Ghost ever wholly withheld, where the gospel is preached with power, and men are alive to God. For your sake - Seeking your advantage, not our own.
Though in much affliction, yet with much joy.

For from you the word sounded forth — (Thessalonica being a city of great commerce.) Being echoed, as it were, from you. And your conversion was divulged far beyond Macedonia and Achaia. So that we need not speak anything - Concerning it.
For they themselves — The people wherever we come.

Whom he hath raised from the dead — In proof of his future coming to judgment. Who delivereth us - He redeemed us once; he delivers us continually; and will deliver all that believe from the wrath, the eternal vengeance, which will then come upon the ungodly.

glossa.text: *Silvanus and Timothy.* The salutation is prefixed with their names, but the sense and the words of this epistle are the Apostle's alone.

*Grace be to you and peace.* After his custom he sets the salutation first, and this being set first, he gives thanks for their good things, calling to mind not only their faith and works, but also the manner of their conversion and their endurance of evils.
*Before God.* Thence [you are] so certain as though you already saw; and thus he encourages them.

*In the Holy Spirit.* Because through me you received the gifts of the Spirit, not sparingly, but in fullness. *What manner of men we were,* etc. By this also, that we have suffered for an example to you, it is plain that God has loved and chosen you.

notes.text: Mark xii, 13; Luke xx, 20.

The Herodians were a set of men peculiarly attached to Herod, and consequently zealous for the interest of the Roman government, which was the main support of the dignity and royalty of his family. Thou regardest not the person of men — Thou favourest no man for his riches or greatness.

Is it lawful to give tribute to Caesar? — If he had said, Yes, the Pharisees would have accused him to the people, as a betrayer of the liberties of his country. If he had said, No, the Herodians would have accused him to the Roman governor.
Ye hypocrites — Pretending a scruple of conscience.
The tribute money — A Roman coin, stamped with the head of Caesar, which was usually paid in tribute.

They say to him, Caesar's — Plainly acknowledging, by their having received his coin, that they were under his government. And indeed this is a standing rule. The current coin of every nation shows who is the supreme governor of it. Render therefore, ye Pharisees, to Caesar the things which ye yourselves acknowledge to be Ciaesar's: and, ye Herodians, while ye are zealous for Caesar, see that ye render to God the things that are God's.

glossa.text:
*With the Herodians, saying.* As though to men unknown, that they might the more easily deceive, because they feared the crowds. What they dare not by themselves, they attempt by the governor's hands. *With the Herodians.* That is, with the soldiers of Herod. Under Caesar Augustus, when the enrolment was made, Judea was made tributary. Over these tributes was set Herod the son of Antipater, an alien and a proselyte, appointed king for the Jews by Augustus. There was therefore sedition among the people, some saying that tributes ought to be given, for security and quiet, since the Romans bear arms for all. The Pharisees striving against it, that the people of God, which pays tithes and the rest that the law prescribes, ought not to lie under human laws. The Pharisees therefore send to see whether they might deceive him.

*Thou hast no care,* etc. To this they provoke him, that he should fear God more than Caesar: and therefore should say that tributes ought not to be paid, so that the Herodians might hold him as the author of sedition.
*Hypocrites.* Because they are one thing and feign another.
*Render therefore.* Or, as Caesar exacts the stamping of his own image, so also does God the soul signed with the light of his countenance.

echoes.text: ‘Yahweh bless you, and keep you. Yahweh make his face to shine on you, and be gracious to you. Yahweh lift up his face toward you, and give you peace.’
echoes.note: Paul's epistolary 'Grace to you and peace' fuses a Greek salutation with the Hebrew shalom; the doubled blessing of grace/favor and peace recalls the Aaronic benediction where YHWH makes his face shine (grace) and gives peace. Volume is low and the wording is Pauline convention, so the echo is faint, but Availability and Coherence with a Jewish blessing idiom support a thin resonance.

echoes.text: Yes, in the way of your judgments, Yahweh, have we waited for you. Your name and your renown are the desire of our soul.
echoes.note: The triad work-of-faith, labor-of-love, and 'patience (endurance) of hope' before God resonates with Isaiah's posture of waiting for YHWH's name in the path of his judgments, the soul's desire and hope. The conceptual overlap (steadfast hope directed toward God) is real but the verbal volume is minimal, so this is a contested coherence-driven echo.

echoes.text: For you are a holy people to Yahweh your God. Yahweh your God has chosen you to be a people for his own possession, above all peoples who are on the face of the earth. Yahweh didn’t set his love on you, nor choose you, because you were more in number than any people; for you were the fewest of all peoples: but because Yahweh loves you, and because he desires to keep the oath which he swore to your fathers, Yahweh has brought you out with a mighty hand, […]
echoes.note: 'Brothers loved by God, that you are chosen' transposes Israel's covenant election directly: Deuteronomy says YHWH chose Israel not for their merit but because he loved them (agapan/eklegesthai LXX), the exact pairing of divine love and choosing Paul applies to gentile believers. Volume and Coherence are strong, and Recurrence of the election theme through 1 Thess makes this a programmatic allusion.

echoes.text: Blessed is the nation whose God is Yahweh, the people whom he has chosen for his own inheritance.
echoes.note: 'Blessed is the nation whose God is YHWH, the people he has chosen for his own inheritance' supplies the same election idiom Paul extends to the Thessalonian assembly. The LXX exelexato matches Paul's vocabulary of being chosen; Volume is moderate and the allusion reinforces the Deuteronomic election frame.

echoes.text: “But you, Israel, my servant, Jacob whom I have chosen, the seed of Abraham my friend, You whom I have taken hold of from the ends of the earth, and called from its corners, and said to you, ‘You are my servant, I have chosen you and not cast you away;’
echoes.note: 'Israel my servant, Jacob whom I have chosen, offspring of Abraham my beloved... I have chosen you and not cast you off' clusters chosenness and divine love exactly as Paul does. The dense overlap of election + beloved makes this a plausible secondary source alongside Deuteronomy 7.

echoes.text: The Spirit of the Lord Yahweh is on me; because Yahweh has anointed me to preach good news to the humble. He has sent me to bind up the broken hearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives, and release to those who are bound;
echoes.note: The gospel coming 'not in word only, but also in power and in the Holy Spirit' echoes the Spirit-anointed proclamation of good news (the LXX euangelisasthai with the Spirit of the Lord upon the herald). Coherence with Paul's evangel-in-Spirit is strong; verbal volume is moderate, supporting an echo of the Isaianic herald.
echoes.lxxText: The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he has anointed me; he has sent me to preach glad tidings to the poor, to heal the broken in heart, to proclaim liberty to the captives, and recovery of sight to the blind;

echoes.text: About Benjamin he said, “The beloved of Yahweh will dwell in safety by him. He covers him all day long. He dwells between his shoulders.”
echoes.note: 'Beloved of YHWH' (Benjamin) as a covenant epithet underlies Paul's address 'brothers loved by God.' The phrase is a stock Septuagintal way of naming the elect community; faint by itself but coherent with the surrounding election language.

echoes.text: But as for me, I am full of power by the Spirit of Yahweh, and of judgment, and of might, to declare to Jacob his disobedience, and to Israel his sin.
echoes.note: 'I am full of power by the Spirit of YHWH' pairs power and Spirit as the equipment of true proclamation, the same coupling Paul uses to validate his preaching against mere word. The dyad is suggestive but the link is contested given how common power/Spirit language is.

echoes.text: Therefore with joy you will draw water out of the wells of salvation.
echoes.note: 'Received the word in much affliction, with joy of the Holy Spirit' resonates with the prophetic motif of drawing joy from God amid distress (e.g., joy from the wells of salvation). The eschatological-Spirit joy-in-affliction pattern is broadly Septuagintal; volume is low, so this is a faint coherence echo.

echoes.text: Many peoples shall go and say, “Come, let’s go up to the mountain of Yahweh, to the house of the God of Jacob; and he will teach us of his ways, and we will walk in his paths.” For out of Zion the law shall go out, and Yahweh’s word from Jerusalem.
echoes.note: 'From you the word of the Lord has been declared... in every place' echoes the Zion oracle in which the word of YHWH goes forth from Jerusalem to the nations. Paul recasts the believing community as a new radiating center for the logos kyriou; Coherence with the mission-of-the-word theme is strong though the geography is reapplied.

echoes.text: so shall my word be that goes out of my mouth: it shall not return to me void, but it shall accomplish that which I please, and it shall prosper in the thing I sent it to do.
echoes.note: YHWH's word that 'goes out' from his mouth and does not return empty but accomplishes its purpose underlies the image of the word of the Lord sounding forth and bearing fruit everywhere. The 'going out' verb and effectual-word theology cohere, but the verbal contact is modest.

echoes.text: Their voice has gone out through all the earth, their words to the end of the world. In them he has set a tent for the sun,
echoes.note: 'Their voice has gone out into all the earth' is the classic text for a proclamation diffusing universally (cited at Romans 10:18). The 'gone out into every place' phrasing of Paul's report shares this diffusion imagery; faint but availability and coherence warrant noting.

echoes.text: For from the rising of the sun even to the going down of the same, my name is great among the nations, and in every place incense will be offered to my name, and a pure offering: for my name is great among the nations,” says Yahweh of Armies.
echoes.note: 'In every place' offerings are made to YHWH's name 'from the rising of the sun to its setting' supplies the universalizing 'in every place' formula Paul uses for the spread of faith toward God. The phrase is a Septuagintal marker of the name's worldwide honor; contested given its commonness.

echoes.text: But Yahweh is the true God; he is the living God, and an everlasting King: at his wrath the earth trembles, and the nations are not able to withstand his indignation.
echoes.note: 'A living and true God' set against 'idols' renders Jeremiah's contrast: 'YHWH is the true God; he is the living God' over against the worthless idols of the nations. Jeremiah 10 is the locus classicus of the idol-polemic Paul compresses; Volume, Coherence, and the living/true pairing make this a strong allusion.

echoes.text: Their idols are silver and gold, the work of men’s hands. They have mouths, but they don’t speak. They have eyes, but they don’t see. They have ears, but they don’t hear. They have noses, but they don’t smell. They have hands, but they don’t feel. They have feet, but they don’t walk, neither do they speak through their throat. Those who make them will be like them; yes, everyone who trusts in them.
echoes.note: 'You turned to God from idols' draws on the satire of manufactured idols (silver and gold, the work of human hands, with mouths that cannot speak) versus the living God. The turning-from-idols-to-serve-God movement is the Psalm's polemic inverted into conversion language; high coherence and strong Septuagintal availability.

echoes.text: Everyone who makes an engraved image is vain. The things that they delight in will not profit. Their own witnesses don’t see, nor know, that they may be disappointed. Who has fashioned a god, or molds an image that is profitable for nothing? Behold, all his fellows will be disappointed; and the workmen are mere men. Let them all be gathered together. Let them stand up. They will fear. They will be put to shame together. The blacksmith takes an ax, works […]
echoes.note: Isaiah's extended mockery of idol-makers who fashion lifeless gods is the deutero-Isaianic counterpart Paul presupposes in 'turned to God from idols.' The dead-idols vs. living-God antithesis is the engine of the verse; Recurrence of this polemic across Second-Temple Judaism strengthens the allusion.

echoes.text: That day is a day of wrath, a day of distress and anguish, a day of trouble and ruin, a day of darkness and gloom, a day of clouds and blackness,
echoes.note: 'The wrath to come' from which Jesus delivers draws on the Day of YHWH as 'a day of wrath' (the orge of the Lord); Zephaniah 1:15,18 is the densest concentration of day-of-wrath language Paul presupposes for the coming eschatological judgment. Coherence with Pauline orge and Recurrence of the wrath motif in 1 Thess (2:16; 5:9) make this a primary allusion.

echoes.text: I make a decree, that in all the dominion of my kingdom men tremble and fear before the God of Daniel; for he is the living God, and steadfast forever, His kingdom that which shall not be destroyed; and his dominion shall be even to the end.
echoes.note: Darius's decree that all should fear 'the living God... who endures forever' supplies the 'living God' confession that gentiles are summoned to serve. The phrase 'living God' is the verbal anchor; Daniel's gentile-king acknowledgment coheres with Paul's report of gentile turning to the living and true God.

echoes.text: You shall fear Yahweh your God; and you shall serve him, and shall swear by his name.
echoes.note: 'To serve a living and true God' picks up the Shema-context command to fear YHWH and serve (latreuein) him only, the exclusive-service demand that idolatry violates. The Deuteronomic 'serve him alone' is the positive correlate of turning from idols; coherence is strong, volume moderate.

echoes.text: Neither their silver nor their gold will be able to deliver them in the day of Yahweh’s wrath, but the whole land will be devoured by the fire of his jealousy; for he will make an end, yes, a terrible end, of all those who dwell in the land.
echoes.note: 'In the day of YHWH's wrath... the whole earth shall be consumed' supplies the universal, future, fiery character of 'the wrath to come.' Reinforces 1:15 as the Day-of-the-Lord matrix from which deliverance is needed.

echoes.text: Yahweh thunders his voice before his army; for his forces are very great; for he is strong who obeys his command; for the day of Yahweh is great and very awesome, and who can endure it?
echoes.note: 'The day of YHWH is great and very terrible; who can endure it?' frames the coming wrath as the dreadful Day from which one must be rescued. Joel's rhetorical question about enduring the Day undergirds Paul's promise that Jesus 'delivers us'; coherence is strong, verbal volume moderate.

echoes.text: Behold, the day of Yahweh comes, cruel, with wrath and fierce anger; to make the land a desolation, and to destroy its sinners out of it.
echoes.note: 'The day of YHWH comes, cruel, with wrath and fierce anger, to make the earth a desolation' is a paradigmatic Day-of-wrath oracle feeding Paul's 'wrath to come.' The eschatological orge directed at the nations coheres with the deliverance of believers; a solid secondary source for the wrath motif.

echoes.text: “But who can endure the day of his coming? And who will stand when he appears? For he is like a refiner’s fire, and like launderer’s soap;
echoes.note: 'Who can endure the day of his coming?' couples the coming (the One who comes) with refining judgment, resonating with waiting for the Son who delivers from the coming wrath. The 'who can endure' topos and the link of advent + judgment make this a coherent echo within the Day-of-the-Lord cluster.

echoes.text: Now for a long time Israel was without the true God, and without a teaching priest, and without law.
echoes.note: 'For a long time Israel was without the true God' uses the precise phrase 'true God' that Paul applies to the object of conversion. A faint but genuine Septuagintal source for 'true God' alongside Jeremiah 10.

echoes.text: Come, my people, enter into your rooms, and shut your doors behind you. Hide yourself for a little moment, until the indignation is past. For, behold, Yahweh comes out of his place to punish the inhabitants of the earth for their iniquity. The earth also will disclose her blood, and will no longer cover her slain.
echoes.note: 'Hide yourselves... until the wrath (orge) is past, for YHWH comes out to punish' offers the motif of being sheltered from passing wrath, paralleling deliverance 'from the wrath to come.' Faint verbal contact but apt coherence with rescue-from-wrath; contested.

echoes.text: I will tell of the decree. Yahweh said to me, “You are my son. Today I have become your father.
echoes.note: 'To wait for his Son from heaven' reads the enthroned royal Son ('You are my Son') figurally of the risen Jesus whose advent executes divine judgment, the Psalm whose next verses warn the nations of the Son's wrath. The Son-language plus impending judgment coheres figurally, though Paul does not cite it here; marked low and contested.

echoes.text: I saw in the night visions, and behold, there came with the clouds of the sky one like a son of man, and he came even to the ancient of days, and they brought him near before him.
echoes.note: Waiting for the Son to come 'from heaven' to deliver at the judgment evokes the one like a son of man coming with the clouds to receive dominion at the eschatological assize. The heavenly-advent-and-judgment pattern is figurally apposite, though the explicit Son-of-Man title is absent here; faint, contested.

echoes.attribution: Catena, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wilson Pruitt / Wroot Press)

echoes.text: God created man in his own image. In God’s image he created him; male and female he created them.
echoes.note: Jesus' question 'whose image (eikon) and inscription?' (22:20) plays on imago Dei: the coin bears Caesar's image and is owed to Caesar, but humanity bears God's image and is owed wholly to God — 'render to God the things that are God's' (22:21).

echoes.text: The earth is Yahweh’s, with its fullness; the world, and those who dwell therein.
echoes.note: 'The earth is the LORD's, and the fulness thereof' — undergirds the claim that what is God's (everything, including the bearer of his image) belongs to God (22:21).

echoes.text: I say, “Keep the king’s command!” because of the oath to God.
echoes.note: Counsel to keep the king's commandment because of one's oath to God — faint wisdom backdrop to the dual obligation to Caesar and to God (22:21).

doctrine.title: Nicene Creed
doctrine.article: the life of the world to come

registers.label: Spare
lines: Whose image is this? Caesar's. Then give to God what is God's.
We bear God's image; to God we belong.
I am the Lord, and there is no other.
Sing to the Lord a new song; the Lord reigns.
The nations and their coins are not our king.
Declare God's glory among the peoples.
Come, let us worship the One who alone is Lord.
We give ourselves to God. Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: Hold a coin in your hand and read the face stamped on it, then look at the face beside you, stamped with the image of God.
The Lord reigns; sing a new song.
Give Caesar his coins and his due, but give to God what bears God's likeness — give God yourself.
The Lord reigns; sing a new song.
For there is no other: not Cyrus, not Caesar, not any throne under heaven; the Lord forms the light and the dark.
The Lord reigns; sing a new song.
Declare his glory among the nations, his marvelous works among all the peoples.
The Lord reigns; sing a new song.
So come, you who bear his image, and worship.
The Lord reigns; sing a new song. Let the earth rejoice!

registers.label: Hybrid
lines: Whose image is on the coin? And whose image do you bear?
We belong to God; the Lord reigns.
I am the Lord, and there is no other.
We belong to God; the Lord reigns.
Give Caesar his coins; give God yourself.
We belong to God; the Lord reigns.
Come, let us sing the Lord a new song.
We give ourselves to God. Amen.
